consensus.consensusInference: The CPC's October 8 outlook lifted the historic-event probability to 83% (from 75% in September and 69% in August): an 83% chance the 3-month RONI reaches ≥+2.5°C during Oct–Dec, exceeding every El Niño since 1950, with 70% for Nov–Jan. IRI's mid-October plume is unanimous — all 27 models forecast very strong from OND through DJF, the multimodel average peaks near +3.5°C, and about 10 models reach or exceed +3.5°C, beyond IRI's highest category. El Niño probability is 100% from OND 2026 through MAM 2027. The forecast has converged completely; the only remaining question is the size of the record, with 2015-16's +2.6°C ONI peak the mark to beat.

timeline.inference: These are official IRI probabilities that El Niño is present in each 3-month season, not its strength. El Niño probability is 100% from OND 2026 through MAM 2027, then 92% (AMJ), 60% (MJJ) and 37% (JJA 2027, when ENSO-neutral becomes most likely at 51%). The decline through spring–summer 2027 is the expected end-of-event decay, consistent with strong events weakening rapidly after peak — not a weakening now. Strength is at its ceiling (83% historic). Both hold: near-certain through the 2026–27 winter, projected to peak near +3.5°C, and expected to fade to neutral by mid-2027.
